This work analyzes and quantifies the characteristics of two video anomaly datasets to better understand the difficulties of pose-based anomaly detection, and takes a step forward in exploring the discriminating power of pose and trajectory for video anomaly detection and their effectiveness based on context. ### Human-Centric Video Anomaly Detection Through Spatio-Temporal Pose Tokenization and Transformer. ### Semantic Features Extraction for Anomaly Detection from Real-World Videos\*. This paper proposes a method to detect anomalies from video while providing a semantic explanation of the cause, and introduces new postural descriptions and time series descriptions of poses using a spatiotemporal graph convolutional neural network. ### Dual-Space Normalizing Flow for Unsupervised Video Anomaly Detection. 2020 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and…. A new method for anomaly detection of human actions that works directly on human pose graphs that can be computed from an input video sequence, and performs considerably better than other state of the art methods. ### Unsupervised video anomaly detection via normalizing flows with implicit latent features. 2022 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and…. This work proposes a novel unsupervised Generative Cooperative Learning (GCL) approach for video anomaly detection that exploits the low frequency of anomalies towards building a cross-supervision between a generator and a discriminator. ### Real-World Anomaly Detection in Surveillance Videos. 2018 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and…. 2022 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and…. UB-normal is the first video anomaly detection benchmark to allow a fair head-to-head comparison between one-class open-set models and supervised closed- set models, and empirical evidence showing that UB-normal can enhance the performance of a state-of-the-art anomaly detection framework on two prominent data sets, Avenue and ShanghaiTech. 2020 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and…. This paper proposes to tackle the anomaly detection problem within a video prediction framework by introducing a motion (temporal) constraint in video prediction by enforcing the optical flow between predicted frames and ground truth frames to be consistent, and is the first work that introduces a temporal constraint into the video prediction task.

results.content: A Comprehensive Guide to Normalizing Flows in Machine Learning and Deep Learning Sarah Lee AI generated Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8 5 min read· June 10, 2025 Photo by Steinar Engeland on Unsplash Normalizing Flows is a class of deep generative models that have gained significant attention in the machine learning community due to their ability to model complex distributions and perform density estimation. ### Definition and Basic Concepts Normalizing Flows are a type of generative model that uses a sequence of invertible transformations to map a simple base distribution to a complex target distribution. ### History and Evolution of Normalizing Flows The concept of Normalizing Flows dates back to the 2010s, when researchers began exploring the idea of using invertible transformations to model complex distributions. Normalizing Flows offer a unique trade-off between these two models, providing both efficient density estimation and sampling capabilities. ### Density Estimation and Sampling Normalizing Flows allow for efficient density estimation and sampling from the target distribution. The density estimation is performed using the change of variables formula, while sampling is done by transforming a random sample from the base distribution using the inverse of the Normalizing Flow. ### Loss Functions and Optimization The loss function used to train Normalizing Flows is typically the negative log-likelihood of the data: L(θ)=−∑i=1 N log⁡p(x i;θ)\mathcal{L}(\theta) = -\sum_{i=1}^N \log p(\mathbf{x}_i; \theta)L(θ)=−i=1∑N​lo g p(x i​;θ) where θ\theta θ are the model parameters, and x i\mathbf{x}_i x i​ are the data points. Normalizing Flows have a wide range of applications in machine learning, including image and audio generation, reinforcement learning, and anomaly detection. ### Image and Audio Generation Normalizing Flows can be used to model complex distributions over images and audio data. Normalizing Flows are a powerful tool in machine learning, offering efficient density estimation and sampling capabilities. ### What are Normalizing Flows? Normalizing Flows are a type of deep generative model that uses a sequence of invertible transformations to map a simple base distribution to a complex target distribution. Normalizing Flows offer efficient density estimation and sampling capabilities, making them suitable for a wide range of applications. Normalizing Flows have been used for image and audio generation, reinforcement learning, variational inference, and anomaly detection.

results.content: # Anomaly Detection using Contrastive Normalizing Flows. Detecting test data deviating from training data is a central problem for. safe and robust machine learning. Likelihoods learned by a generative model,. e.g., a normalizing flow via standard log-likelihood training, perform poorly. We propose to use an unlabelled auxiliary dataset and a. probabilistic outlier score for anomaly detection. results.content: NanoFlow: Scalable Normalizing Flows with Sublinear Parameter Complexity Sang-gil Lee Sungwon Kim Sungroh Yoon∗ Data Science & AI Lab. Seoul National University {tkdrlf9202, ksw0306, sryoon}@snu.ac.kr Abstract Normalizing ﬂows (NFs) have become a prominent method for deep generative models that allow for an analytic probability density estimation and efﬁcient syn-thesis. The decomposed view on building ﬂow-based models with NanoFlow suggests that two directions can be endeavored in future research: composing more expressive bijections, which has been the primary focus in existing literature, and building an optimized neural density estimator that can potentially provide a more adaptive computation path leveraged by ﬂow indication embedding.

# FastFlow: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection and Localization via 2D Normalizing Flows. title={FastFlow: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection and Localization via 2D Normalizing Flows},. This work proposes FastFlow implemented with 2D normalizing flows and uses it as the probability distribution estimator for unsupervised anomaly detection and localization and achieves 99.4% AUC in anomaly detection with high inference efficiency. ### Self-Supervised Normalizing Flows for Image Anomaly Detection and Localization. Li-Ling ChiuShang-Hong Lai. 2023 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and…. A novel two-stage framework is proposed in this paper to build anomaly estimators with normal data only and model the distribution of training data on the learned representations as the one-class classifier to detect anomaly. This work designs a new feature fusion module in the normalizing flow model to integrate texture features and semantic features, which can substantially improve the fitting of the distribution function with input data, thus achieving improved performance for the detection of both types of anomalies. 2023 IEEE/CVF International Conference on…. Daehyun KimSun-Mee BaikTae Hyun Kim. This work trains NF to map the feature distributions of normal data to different distributions at each location in the given image to enhance the discriminability and highlight the efficacy of the proposed framework in improving the density modeling and thus anomaly detection performance. A real-time model based on a conditional normalizing flow frame- work adopted for anomaly detection with localization that is faster and smaller by a factor of 10× than prior state-of-the-art with the same input setting and outperforms previous methods. ### Modeling the Distribution of Normal Data in Pre-Trained Deep Features for Anomaly Detection. This work introduces the MVTec Anomaly Detection (MVTec AD) dataset containing 5354 high-resolution color images of different object and texture categories, and conducts a thorough evaluation of current state-of-the-art unsupervised anomaly detection methods based on deep architectures such as convolutional autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, and feature descriptors using pre-trained convolved neural networks. This work presents a novel anomaly segmentation approach based on alignment between an anomalous image and a constant number of the similar normal images, which is shown to achieve state-of-the-art performance on unsupervised anomaly detection and localization while requiring virtually no training time.
